q: 1. In which year the term 'Sustainable Development' came into existence?
explain: The term was first introduced in the World Conservation Strategy (WCS) in 1980, though it was later popularized by the Brundtland Report in 1987.

q: 2. Which famous report on sustainable development was titled 'Our Common Future'?
explain: The Brundtland Report, published in 1987 by the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED), is formally titled 'Our Common Future'.

q: 3. When was Sustainable Development policy introduced in Nepal?
explain: Nepal formally integrated sustainable development concepts and environmental impact assessments during the 8th Five Year Plan (1992–1997).

q: 4. What is/are core element(s) of Sustainable Development?
explain: Sustainable development is built on three main pillars: economic viability, social equity, and environmental protection.

q: 5. How many Sustainable Development Goals have been set by the United Nations Sustainable Development Summit - 2015?
explain: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, adopted by all UN Member States in 2015, defines 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

q: 6. The international organizations are working with ______ to meet SDG goals.
explain: Achieving the SDGs requires a multi-stakeholder partnership involving governments, the private sector, and civil society (Goal 17).

q: 7. Among the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, 13th Goal is
explain: Goal 13 specifically calls for urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.

q: 8. Who was first coined the term "Sustainable Development"?
explain: Barbara Ward is often credited with pioneering the concept in the 1970s, emphasizing the link between economic development and environmental care.

q: 9. Which statement depicts the best definition of sustainable development?
options: It means optimal utilization of natural resources.
Sustainable use of natural resources without considering the need of the future generation
Present generation fulfills its needs while consider the needs of the future generation as well
explain: The classic definition is development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

q: 10. The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development Goals acknowledge that all governments must Promote action in:
options: People, Planet, Prosperity, Peace and Partnership
People, Environment, Prosperity, Peace and Foresight
explain: These are known as the '5 Ps' that inform the SDGs: People, Planet, Prosperity, Peace, and Partnership.

q: 11. Among the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, which of the following goal is not related to with Nepal?
explain: As a landlocked country, Goal 14 (Life Below Water), which focuses on oceans and marine resources, is not directly applicable to Nepal's geography.

q: 12. How many targets have been set by sustainable development goals to eliminate all kinds of poverty and hunger by 2030 A.D.?
explain: The 17 Sustainable Development Goals are accompanied by 169 specific targets to be achieved by 2030.

q: 13. "We don't have plan B because there is no planet B." Whose Statement is this regarding to the development of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)?
explain: This famous quote was delivered by former UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon to emphasize the urgency of climate action.

q: 14. In which year, the millennium development goals (MDGs) declared by the United Nations (UN)?
explain: The MDGs were established following the Millennium Summit of the United Nations in 2000.

q: 15. The first Earth summit was held at -----------
explain: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), also known as the Earth Summit, was held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.

q: 16. --------, came out as a part of Earth Summit 1992.
explain: Agenda 21 is a comprehensive plan of action to be taken globally, nationally, and locally by organizations of the UN, which was a major outcome of the 1992 Earth Summit.

q: 17. Agenda-21 related --------
explain: Agenda 21 is a non-binding action plan of the United Nations with regard to sustainable development.

q: 18. The first country to sign in Agenda 21 is ---------
explain: China was one of the earliest and most prominent signatories to commit to the implementation of Agenda 21.

q: 19. During which plan period, the Environmental protection act and Rules were enacted and enforced in Nepal?
explain: The Environment Protection Act (2053) and Rules (2054) were enacted during the 8th Plan period in Nepal.

q: 20. Where is headquarters of United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) located?
explain: UNEP is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, making it one of the few UN agencies based in a developing nation.

q: 21. Earth watch is related to ----------
explain: Earthwatch Institute is an international non-profit organization that focuses on environmental conservation through scientific field research.

q: 22. The first environment day in Nepal was observed in?
explain: Nepal began celebrating World Environment Day in 1976, following the global trend started in 1974.

q: 23. Which country has been started the movement of "Earth hour"?
explain: Earth Hour started as a lights-off event in Sydney, Australia, in 2007, organized by WWF-Australia.

q: 24. Which of the following is correct slogan regarding International Environment Day - 2025 celebrated on 5th June every year?
options: Save the earth, save our environment
explain: As per the answer key provided in the book, the slogan for 2025 is 'Save the earth, save our environment'.

q: 25. The Theme of 'Earth day' 2025 is;
explain: The answer key specifies 'Our Power, Our Planet' as the theme for Earth Day 2025.

q: 26. Earth hour 2025 was celebrated throughout the world to combat climate change and protect biodiversity and nature. What edition of 'Earth Hour' was it?
explain: Counting from its inception in 2007, the 2025 event marks the 19th edition of Earth Hour.

q: 27. Which one agenda is not related with Earth Summit, 1992 AD?
explain: Global 500 was an award program started in 1987 by UNEP, whereas the others were formal outcomes or topics of the 1992 Summit.

q: 28. Which ISO specifies audit protocol of environment?
explain: ISO 14064 provides specifications for the quantification, monitoring, and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions and removals.

q: 29. Who is the founder of Green Belt Movement?
explain: The Green Belt Movement was founded by Nobel Laureate Wangari Maathai in Kenya in 1977.

q: 30. Who is awarded WWF Conservation Award 2020 A.D.?
explain: Rinzin Phunjok Lama, a Nepali conservationist, was recognized for his work in the high-altitude Himalayas.

q: 31. Who received Blue Planet Award 2024 A.D.?
explain: Professor Robert Costanza is recognized for his pioneering work in ecological economics.

q: 32. The Goldman award is related to;
explain: The Goldman Environmental Prize is awarded annually to grassroots environmental activists.

q: 33. Who was the first Nepali to receive the Global-500 award?
explain: Dr. Krishna Kumar Pandey was the first Nepali to be honored with the UNEP Global 500 award for environmental achievement.

q: 34. Global 500 'awards are given for the outstanding achievement in which of the following fields?
explain: The Global 500 Roll of Honour was a tribute to environmental achievers from around the world.

q: 35. When World Wildlife Fund was established?
explain: WWF was founded on April 29, 1961, in Morges, Switzerland.

q: 36. Who published the "Red Data Book" about the list of rare animals?
explain: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) maintains and publishes the Red List of Threatened Species.

q: 37. Currently, How many countries have signed the CITES treaty?
explain: As of recent counts reflected in the textbook, 184 parties (including the EU) have joined the CITES treaty.

q: 38. Organization related to 'Red Data Book' or 'Red List' is -------
explain: As noted in question 36, IUCN is the authority responsible for the Red List.

q: 39. CITES is related to ----------
options: Protection of Endangered species of wild Flora and Fauna
explain: CITES stands for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora.

q: 40. Which of the following pairs is wrong?
explain: WWF was established in 1961, not 1960, making option (a) the incorrect pair.

q: 41. World Wildlife fund was established in --------
explain: Reconfirming the date from question 35, WWF was founded in 1961.

q: 42. Which Country is not included in ICIMOD?
explain: The eight member countries of ICIMOD are Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, and Pakistan. Thailand is not a member.

q: 43. Which of the following is incorrect?
explain: World Environment Day was established in 1972 but first celebrated in 1974.

q: 44. Sound is said to be hazardous when its Intensity is above ---------
explain: Prolonged exposure to noise levels above 80-85 decibels (dB) can lead to permanent hearing damage.

q: 45. Which one of the following is not a secondary Pollutant?
explain: Sulphur dioxide (SO2) is a primary pollutant because it is emitted directly from a source. The others are formed through chemical reactions in the atmosphere.

q: 46. Kyoto protocol (1997) is related with ----------
options: Reduction of emission of green house gas
explain: The Kyoto Protocol is an international treaty that committed state parties to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

q: 47. The concept of 'Carbon credit' originated from:
explain: The Kyoto Protocol introduced the market-based mechanisms of carbon credits to help countries reach emission targets.

q: 48. Which country in the world responsible for largest percentage of global house gas (GHG) emissions?
explain: China is currently the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases due to its large population and industrial base.

q: 49. 'Montreal Protocol' is related to ---------
explain: The Montreal Protocol is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of substances like CFCs.

q: 50. When did Nepal signed Paris Agreement?
explain: Nepal signed the Paris Agreement on the very first day it opened for signature, April 22, 2016.

q: 51. According to IPCC, what part in the world, Nepal contributes greenhouse gas emission?
explain: According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), Nepal's share of global greenhouse gas emissions is approximately 0.027%.

q: 52. According to the Recent study conducted by department of hydrology and metrology, the average maximum temperature of Nepal has risen by ----------
explain: Studies by the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) indicate an annual increase in maximum temperature of about 0.056°C in Nepal.

q: 53. How long has Nepal declared its commitment to zero emission strategy (Zero Net Strategy) at the Glasgow conference on climate change in 2021?
explain: At COP26 in Glasgow, Nepal committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2045.

q: 54. Who was coined the term Global warming?
explain: Wallace 'Wally' Broecker popularized the term 'Global Warming' in a 1975 scientific paper.

q:
55. Consider the following Statement & Choose the correct one: 
 I. The Earth Summit 1992 issued United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) 
 II. 10-10-10 is related to climate change.
explain: The UNFCCC was a major outcome of the 1992 Earth Summit, and '10-10-10' refers to a global day of climate action held on October 10, 2010.

q: 56. UNFCCC COP -29 conferences, Baku, Azerbaijan focused on ----------
options: The reduction of Green house & its emission
explain: The COP29 summit in Baku is heavily focused on setting a new global goal for climate finance to support developing nations.

q: 57. Which One of the following is the main objective of Vienna Convention and its Montreal protocol?
explain: The Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol are international agreements specifically designed to phase out substances that deplete the ozone layer.

q: 58. Which of the following Greenhouse Gases has the highest atmospheric lifetime?
explain: Sulphur Hexafluoride (SF6) is extremely stable and can remain in the atmosphere for over 3,000 years.

q: 59. The one which isn't considered as naturally occurring green house greenhouse gas is --------
explain: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are entirely man-made (synthetic) chemicals and do not occur naturally.

q: 60. Which one of the following pairs of gases are the major causes of "Green House Effect"?
explain: Carbon dioxide (CO2) and Methane (CH4) are the two most significant contributors to the anthropogenic greenhouse effect.

q: 61. Which one of the following is mainly responsible for green house effect?
explain: While many gases contribute, CO2 is the primary driver of climate change due to the sheer volume released by human activity.

q: 62. Which of the following is true for the relative contribution of various Green gases to total Global warming?
explain: The magnitude of contribution generally follows the order: Carbon dioxide > Methane > Nitrous Oxide > CFCs.

q: 63. Which of the following is not a green house gas?
explain: Carbon monoxide (CO) is not a direct greenhouse gas, though it can influence the lifetime of other greenhouse gases like methane.

q: 64. Among the following, which gas is the main cause of depletion of ozone layer?
explain: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) release chlorine atoms when broken down by UV radiation, which then catalyze the destruction of ozone molecules.

q: 65. Kyoto Protocol was ratified by Nepal --------
explain: Nepal ratified the Kyoto Protocol on September 16, 2005.

q: 66. Where the UN Climate Change Conference COP 28 held?
explain: COP 28 was hosted by the United Arab Emirates in Dubai in late 2023.

q: 67. Which of the following is not major green house gas?
explain: Nitrogen (N2) makes up 78% of the atmosphere but is not a greenhouse gas because its diatomic molecules do not absorb infrared radiation.

q: 68. Who was the first person to experiment scientifically about the greenhouse effects?
explain: Eunice Newton Foote (1856) and John Tyndall (1859) both independently discovered and experimented on the heat-trapping properties of CO2.

q: 69. When was Kalapathar meeting at foothill of Mt. Everest held to draw the attention of the world regarding the effect of Climate Change?
explain: The Nepal Cabinet held a historic meeting at Kalapathar (5,542m) on December 4, 2009 (Mangsir 19, 2066).

q: 70. Which is the nation to conduct the Cabinet Meeting under the water to gain the attention of the world to reduce the effect of climate change?
explain: The Maldives held an underwater cabinet meeting in 2009 to highlight the threat of rising sea levels to the island nation.

q: 71. 'Kyoto Protocol' is related to --------
explain: The Kyoto Protocol is an international agreement linked to the UNFCCC, specifically aimed at fighting global warming and climate change.

q: 72. Basel convention is related to the --------
options: Trans-boundary Movements of the Hazardous wastes and their disposal
explain: The Basel Convention (1989) regulates the international trade and disposal of hazardous wastes.

q: 73. Which international organization has declared a global climate & environmental emergency?
explain: The European Parliament declared a 'climate and environmental emergency' in Europe and globally in November 2019.

q: 74. When was the first Nepal national wetland Policy issued by the Government?
explain: The first National Wetland Policy of Nepal was formulated in 2053 B.S. (1996) to manage wetland resources sustainably.

q: 75. When was the National Climate Change Policy introduced in Nepal?
explain: The revised National Climate Change Policy was approved in 2076 B.S. (2019), replacing the previous 2067 policy.

q: 76. In which of the following district of Nepal, biodiversity information centre is being established?
explain: A key Biodiversity Information Centre is established at Kasara, Chitwan, within the Chitwan National Park.

q: 77. Which of the following does not fall into category of biodiversity?
explain: Biodiversity typically includes genetic (hereditary), species, and ecosystem (environmental) diversity. 'Climate diversity' describes weather patterns, not biological variety.

q: 78. The largest ecosystem of the earth is --------
explain: The hydrosphere (oceans, seas, lakes) covers about 71% of the Earth's surface, making it the largest ecosystem.

q: 79. What is the theme of World Biodiversity Day 2024 A.D.?
explain: The theme for International Day for Biological Diversity 2024 is 'Be part of the Plan'.

q: 80. How many places of Nepal have been declared wetland now?
explain: As per current Ramsar Convention records, Nepal has 10 sites designated as Wetlands of International Importance.

q: 81. How many kinds of ecosystem are found in Nepal?
explain: The 1988 Biodiversity Strategy identified 118 distinct ecosystems in Nepal across its various physiographic zones.

q: 82. The richest country in the world presented by mongabay.com -2021 in terms of Bio-diversity is
explain: Brazil is consistently ranked as the most biodiverse country in the world due to the Amazon rainforest.

q: 83. Where is the bio-diversity information centre established?
explain: As mentioned in question 76, the centre is located in Chitwan.

q: 84. Which of the following among given richest country is richest in the field of Biodiversity?
explain: Among the options provided, Indonesia holds the highest biodiversity due to its tropical archipelagic nature.

q: 85. According to mongabay.com report-2023, Nepal ranked -------- in the world in term of Biodiversity.
explain: In the Global Biodiversity Index (2023), Nepal is ranked 49th out of nearly 200 countries.

q: 86. 'Bio-diversity Day' is celebrated every year on --------
explain: The United Nations has proclaimed May 22 as the International Day for Biological Diversity.

q: 87. Which of the following component is not related with bio - diversity?
explain: Biodiversity consists of genetic, species, and ecosystem levels. Geographic diversity refers to landforms, not biological variety.

q: 88. The theory of relativity was propounded by --------
explain: Albert Einstein developed the special and general theories of relativity in the early 20th century.

q:
89. Which of the following Statement(s) about famous Scientist Albert Einstein is/are correct? 
 1. He was born in France 
 2. He received Nobel Prize in 1921 A.D. 
 3. He was died in U.S.A.
explain: Einstein was born in Germany (not France), won the Nobel Prize in 1921 for his work on the photoelectric effect, and died in Princeton, USA.

q: 90. Where was the Scientist Stephen Hawking born?
explain: Stephen Hawking was born in Oxford, England, United Kingdom.

q: 91. Who is the writer of "A Brief History of Time: From the Big Bang to Black Hole"?
explain: A Brief History of Time is a popular-science book on cosmology written by Stephen Hawking.

q: 92. In which country "Madam Curie" was born?
explain: Marie Curie was born Maria Sklodowska in Warsaw, Poland.

q: 93. Who is known as "Father of Genetics Science"?
explain: Gregor Mendel is considered the father of genetics for his pioneering work with pea plants.

q: 94. Which is the largest underground atomic laboratory in the world?
explain: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN is the world's largest and most powerful particle accelerator.

q:
95. Identify whether the following statements are correct or incorrect: 
 1. The great Scientist Sir Isaac Newton was born in Britain. 
 2. The first person to land in the Space from United States of America.
explain: Newton was indeed British. However, the first person in space was Yuri Gagarin (USSR), not someone from the USA.

q: 96. Who is the Father of Electricity?
explain: Michael Faraday is known as the father of electricity due to his discoveries of electromagnetic induction and electrolysis.

q: 97. Among the following scientists, who is not related to evolution?
explain: While Darwin and Wallace developed natural selection and Lamarck proposed inheritance of acquired traits, Mendel focused on the laws of inheritance (genetics).

q: 98. Radioactivity was discovered by?
explain: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 while investigating phosphorescence in uranium salts.

q: 99. The Steam engine was invented by --------
explain: James Watt improved Thomas Newcomen's earlier design, creating a more efficient steam engine that powered the Industrial Revolution.

q: 100. Double - helical structure of DNA was given by --------
explain: James Watson and Francis Crick published the correct double-helix model of DNA in 1953.

q: 101. Who invented the e-mail?
explain: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971 and is credited with the use of the '@' symbol to separate the user name from the name of the machine.

q: 102. Who is the first test tube baby of the world?
explain: Louise Joy Brown was the first human to be born after conception by in vitro fertilization (IVF) in 1978.

q: 103. Who was invented Ballpoint pen?
explain: Laszlo Biro and his brother Gyorgy invented the first commercially successful ballpoint pen in 1938.

q: 104. What is the full form of RADAR?
options: Rational Analysis of Damage and Risk
explain: RADAR stands for Radio Detection and Ranging; it uses radio waves to determine the distance, angle, or velocity of objects.

q: 105. Who inverted the penicillin?
explain: Sir Alexander Fleming discovered the antibiotic substance penicillin from the mold Penicillium notatum in 1928.

q: 106. What is the name of first satellite of Nepal?
explain: NepaliSat-1 is a low orbit CubeSat, which was Nepal's first satellite launched in April 2019.

q: 107. Which among the following is not correct?
explain: The printing press was invented by Johannes Gutenberg. Thomas Edison is famous for the light bulb and phonograph.

q: 108. Who invented the calculator?
explain: Blaise Pascal invented the mechanical calculator (Pascaline) in 1642 to help his father with tax computations.

q: 109. Who was the inventor of electric bulb?
explain: Thomas Alva Edison is credited with inventing the first commercially practical incandescent light bulb.

q: 110. Who are the founders of Google Search Engine and Company?
explain: Google was founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin while they were Ph.D. students at Stanford University.

q: 111. Who has written the book, the 'origin of species'?
explain: Charles Darwin's 'On the Origin of Species' (1859) is considered the foundation of evolutionary biology.

q: 112. Who was invented Ballpoint pen?
explain: Repeating question 103, the Biro brothers patented the ballpoint pen design used today.

q: 113. What is the name of new drug developed by Scientist as an alternative to antibiotics?
explain: Staphefect is an engineered enzyme (endolysin) designed to kill specific bacteria like MRSA, often cited as a post-antibiotic alternative.

q: 114. Which of the following is the feature of Fifth Generation Computer?
explain: Fifth-generation computers focus on Artificial Intelligence and may utilize biochips for ultra-fast processing and storage.

q: 115. Who invented the telephone?
explain: Alexander Graham Bell was granted the first US patent for the telephone in 1876.

q: 116. Who is the father of the personal Computer?
explain: Edward Roberts (Henry E. Roberts) is often called the father of the PC after inventing the Altair 8800 in 1974.

q: 117. Who invented the 'Penicillin'?
explain: Repeating question 105, Alexander Fleming's discovery revolutionized medicine and infection control.

q: 118. Who is the English physicist responsible for the "Big Bang Theory"?
explain: While Fr. Georges Lemaître first proposed it, George Gamow developed the theory further, predicting the cosmic microwave background.

q: 119. Who is the Inventor of Watch?
explain: Abraham-Louis Breguet is credited with many innovations in watchmaking, including the tourbillon and early wristwatches.

q:
120. Consider the following matches: 
 1. Printing Press - Johannes Gutenberg 
 2. Radar - Robert Watson Watt 
 3. Television - Alexander Graham bell 
 Which of the above matches is /are correct?
explain: Television was primarily developed by Philo Farnsworth and John Logie Baird, not Alexander Graham Bell (who did telephone).

q: 121. Who is known as the father of Mobile?
explain: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first handheld cellular phone call in 1973.

q: 122. What is the field that the famous scientist Stephen Hawking had significantly contributed to?
explain: Stephen Hawking's work combined general relativity and quantum mechanics, specifically regarding black hole radiation (Hawking Radiation).

q: 123. Who is the current chairman of Twitter, the famous social network?
explain: Elon Musk acquired Twitter in 2022 and took over leadership (later rebranding it to X).

q: 124. The world's smallest gold coin, which features Albert Einstein, is recently released by which country?
explain: Switzerland's state-owned mint released a 2.96 mm gold coin featuring Einstein's face in 2020.

q: 125. Who was awarded Nobel Prize in 1945 for the discovery of penicillin and its curative effects in various infectious diseases?
explain: Fleming shared the 1945 Nobel Prize with Howard Florey and Ernst Boris Chain for their work on penicillin.

q: 126. Match Group I and II...
explain: Mapped from the book's answer key for matching sets.

q: 127. The first successful human Space Flight was -----------
explain: Vostok 1, carrying Yuri Gagarin, was the first spaceflight of the Vostok program and the first human spaceflight in history (1961).

q: 128. The first woman to reach in space is;
explain: Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman to fly in space, orbiting Earth 48 times in Vostok 6 in 1963.

q: 129. Who was the second person to walk on the moon?
explain: Buzz Aldrin followed Neil Armstrong onto the lunar surface during the Apollo 11 mission in 1969.

q: 130. Which was the first country to enter to the Space?
explain: The USSR launched Sputnik 1 in 1957, becoming the first nation to reach space.

q: 131. Which is the first artificial Satellite to orbit Earth?
explain: Sputnik 1 was launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957 as the first artificial Earth satellite.

q: 132. Which of the following space agencies used a Space Craft named Hayabusa?
explain: JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) operated the Hayabusa mission to return samples from an asteroid.

q: 133. From which among the following has Nepal has launched its first Satellite Nepali Sat - I?
explain: NepaliSat-1 was launched from the Mid-Atlantic Regional Spaceport in Virginia, USA.

q: 134. The first flight of the Space Shuttle program by NASA was launched in ----------
explain: The first Space Shuttle flight, STS-1 on Columbia, launched on April 12, 1981.

q: 135. First Person to reach into space was ----------
explain: Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on April 12, 1961.

q: 136. The first human made object to orbit ----------
explain: Sputnik 1 was the first human-made object to achieve Earth orbit.

q: 137. The first successful human Space Flight was ----------
explain: Duplicate of question 127; the answer is Vostok-I.

q: 138. The luna programme was a series of unmanned space mission launched by which country?
explain: The Luna program was a series of robotic spacecraft missions sent to the Moon by the Soviet Union between 1959 and 1976.
